title: Adapting in the Dark: Efficient and Stable Test-Time Adaptation for Black-Box Models
topic: General Machine Learning->Transfer, Multitask and Meta-learning
claim: Models that are most common in practice expose the least access, making adaptation hardest; our setting is the opaque, API-only case.
layout: 3 panels left-to-right, before/after TTA pairs, difficulty arrows top and bottom
description: Three side-by-side beige panels labeled White-Box, Gray-Box and Black-Box. Each panel shows a model box before and after a TTA arrow, with a row of bird image thumbnails below and output arrows above. Before TTA the outputs show mixed green checks and red crosses, and after TTA all are green checks. White-Box shows an open lock and a visible neural network with trainable modules. Gray-Box shows a closed lock, dashed intermediate representations and added modules. Black-Box shows a solid black box with a large padlock, and a white box with a question mark after TTA. A top blue arrow reads 'Real-world Target Model Rarity', from rare to common. A bottom arrow reads 'Difficulty in Improving Downstream Task Performance', from easy to difficult. The eye goes first to the black padlock panel.
caption: The black-box Test-time Adaptation setting studied in this work. From the client's perspective, the goal is to adapt a powerful server-side API model to a target distribution (e.g., corrupted or domain-shifted images) without any internal access. The client can only send raw input images and receive softmax probability vectors in return. Unlike white-box TTA, no gradients, parameters, intermediate features, or architectural details are available, making this a practical yet challenging scenario for real-world API-based deployment.
abstract: Test-Time Adaptation (TTA) for black-box models accessible only via APIs remains a largely unexplored challenge. Existing approaches such as post-hoc output refinement offer limited adaptive capacity, while Zeroth-Order Optimization (ZOO) enables input-space adaptation but faces high query costs and optimization challenges in the unsupervised TTA setting. We introduce BETA (Black-box Efficient Test-time Adaptation), a framework that addresses these limitations by employing a lightweight, local white-box steering model to create a tractable gradient pathway. Through a prediction harmonization technique combined with consistency regularization and prompt learning-oriented filtering, BETA enables stable adaptation with no additional API calls and negligible latency beyond standard inference. On ImageNet-C, BETA achieves a +7.1% accuracy gain on ViT-B/16 and +3.4% on CLIP, surpassing strong white-box and gray-box methods including TENT and TPT. On a commercial API, BETA achieves comparable performance to ZOO at 250x lower cost while maintaining real-time inference speed, establishing it as a practical and efficient solution for real-world black-box TTA.
